hypotheses: Ceritinib is an ALK/ROS1/IGF-1R tyrosine kinase inhibitor; the closest pharmacological match among donors is crizotinib (ALK/ROS1 inhibitor), which has the highest anchor similarity (0.8421) and may reproduce the A375 histone-mark signature.
Regorafenib and sorafenib are multikinase inhibitors with high anchor similarity (0.7386 and 0.7085) and may share downstream chromatin effects with ceritinib despite lower structure similarity.

Ibrutinib (BTK inhibitor) and olmesartan (angiotensin receptor blocker) have moderate anchor similarity (0.4606 and 0.6493) but different mechanisms; they are lower-priority donor candidates for testing whether the histone signature is kinase-class-specific or nonspecific.

The query anchor features show strong positive H3K9me2K14ac0 and H3K4me2 and negative H3K27me1K36me2/H3K27me2K36me2, suggesting a reproducible histone perturbation; donor selection should prioritize compounds with measured A375 responses that can transfer target-minus-A375 values.
object.evidence_gap: No donor has a pharmacology description confirming ALK inhibition or direct histone-modifying activity; ceritinib's histone-mark response at 1 uM/24 h in A375 is not causally linked to ALK/IGF-1R inhibition, and donor anchor similarities are based on a single query signature without independent replication.
